philosophyBody: Simpli keeps English words recognizable, and it uses a small set of regular sounds so people from different languages can understand one another. A sound stays in the language when it is learnable and when losing it would make different words sound the same. English pronunciation is a guide, not a law. An accent is welcome when the words stay distinct.
termWriting: How Simpli is written. The letters and the spelling rules.
termSounds: The sound differences Simpli actually uses. If a difference is not listed here, Simpli does not require it.
termReference: The standard sound, written in the international phonetic alphabet (IPA). Every language version of this page uses the same symbols.
termReal: How a person may actually say that sound. It can differ a little from the reference.
termAccent: A difference that comes from a person’s first language. It is fine when listeners can still tell the words apart.
listenerFlag: Marked items still need a check with listeners.
longer: The same vowel as the single letter, held longer. Do not change it into a different vowel.
glide: One syllable. The tongue glides. This is not two vowels side by side.
lengthGap: A doubled vowel (aa, ee, ii, oo, uu) may be used for extra clarity. In general, it is not: one vowel letter is enough.
vowelO: The vowel of father and hat is a. When English writes that vowel with o, Simpli keeps o: hot, not, and on.
vowelSeq: ai, ei, ao, and oi are one syllable each. ao is the sound in hao and nao; do not write au. Any other pair of vowels is two syllables, as in vidio.
clusterGap: A syllable is often a consonant, a vowel, and an optional consonant. The word list also keeps groups such as str and nk. A short extra vowel is understandable while you learn; the reference pronunciation does not add one. Stress the second-to-last syllable, and do not weaken the other vowels to a mumbled uh.
vwSpell: Write w where English uses w (woter, wi). Write v where English uses v (hav, seven). Prefer the reference sound of each letter.
hKeep: Do not leave this sound out. hand and and, and hav and av, are different words.
rKeep: Do not leave this sound out. A light tap or a short trill is accepted.
lKeep: Keep this sound different from r. long and rong, and lait and rait, are different words.
vwPrefer: Prefer this reference sound for this letter. The other one is widely understood, but veri and weri, wi and vi, and van and wan then sound the same.
tjKeep: Do not replace this with a plain s. tjip and sip are different words.
djKeep: Do not replace this with y or with g. djet and yet, and djet and get, are different words.
rationalePointer: The reference sound of each letter is on the {link}. This page explains which letters Simpli keeps, and why.

art.lipsClosed: Close the lips, then open them.
art.lipsTeeth: Rest the upper teeth on the lower lip.
art.tongueMidFront: Hold the tongue in the middle, toward the front.
art.tongueHighFront: Hold the tongue high and front.
art.tongueMidBack: Hold the tongue in the middle, toward the back.
art.tongueHighBack: Hold the tongue high and back.
art.tongueTip: The tongue tip meets the ridge behind the upper teeth.
art.tongueBack: The back of the tongue meets the soft palate.
art.airStop: Stop the air, then let it go.
art.airNose: Send the air through the nose.
art.airHiss: Force the air through a narrow gap.
art.airSide: Let the air pass along the sides of the tongue.
art.airH: Send a puff of air from the throat. Do not raise the tongue, and do not use f.
art.airR: Bring the tongue tip near the ridge behind the teeth, without a strong trill.
art.airAffricate: Begin with a stop, then release into a hiss at the same place.
art.airGlide: Glide quickly into the following vowel.
